column1: # NORMAN SWEEP, PART 2 -- the 10 EXTREME arms the first 20 did not reach
# Part 1 (scripts/grids/norman_sweep.tsv, job 18363844) bracketed the default:
#   epochs 120-1200 . eta_min 1e-4..1e-3 . batch 256..8192 . loss scale 0.5x/2x
# Every one of those levers had its OPTIMUM AT OR INSIDE the tested range on rhj_fewshot,
# which is exactly the situation F-loss3 flags as a range problem rather than a finished
# tuning. These 10 arms push each lever PAST the part-1 edge, so an endpoint optimum in
# part 1 can be told apart from a true one.
#   eta_min  1e-5, 1e-6, 3e-3   part 1 spans 1e-4..1e-3. The ORIGINAL default was 1e-7,
#                               and 3e-4 only won on rhj at 150 ep -- below and above the
#                               part-1 bracket are both untested on norman.
#   epochs   60, 240            part 1 starts at 120. 60 halves the step budget again;
#                               240 is the far side of rhj's flat 180.
#   batch    128                66,600 steps -- 16x the default's 4,050, the far end of
#                               grid B's step-count hypothesis.
#   scale    0.25x, 4.0x        part 1 is 0.5x/2x around the scale-matched point.
#   lr       3e-4, 3e-3         ⚠️ NEVER VARIED, on either benchmark, in this campaign.
#                               1e-3 came from rhj's W grid where it was raised WITH the
#                               batch size; with 11x fewer steps on norman that pairing has
#                               no reason to hold. decoder_lr tracks it, as in the W grid.
# HOW TO READ IT. Anchors (additive / nonadditive pearson_delta): OCCAM NQ02 published
# experimental 0.9165 / 0.8377.
#   An extreme arm winning  -> part 1's bracket was in the wrong place; re-centre and
#                              re-sweep on that lever.
#   part 1 winning           -> the optimum is INTERIOR and the axis is closed, which is
#                              the result that lets us stop tuning it.
# ⚠️ Read all four metrics. `mae` already splits this field differently from
#    `pearson_delta` (F-comp4), so a pearson_delta-only ranking would mislead.
# COST  10 arms, ~40 GPU-h. All concurrent with part 1.
